title: Arrest model v2: 2-DOF pelvis translation + torso rotation
context: RideBelt is an open, safety-critical Hee-Lee Oss project: an optional rider-worn backup restraint (low hip belt + short tethers; optional clip-on Shoulder Module or one-piece Integrated Harness) that latches into an open seat anchor standard (RAS). ALL safety content is DRAFT and not for use until a credentialed engineer signs off at the MVP gate (GOVERNANCE.md). Never remove a DRAFT banner, never give instructions for wearing or attaching anything to a ride, never copy text from paid standards (cite by number and title only), never name private individuals or incident victims, and respect the patent design-arounds in docs/research/patentability-fto.md. docs/analysis/arrest_model.py is 1-DOF vertical only. It cannot show jackknifing or the upper body rotating out of a hip belt, which drives the shoulder requirements. Risk tier high: requires credentialed expert review before release.
objective: Add a planar 2-DOF model (pelvis held by tethers, torso pivoting at the hip, optional shoulder-strap restraint) with unit tests and a results section.
acceptanceCriteria: v1 results reproduced within 5% when rotation is locked (regression test)
Every assumption (segment masses, inertias, stiffnesses) cited or flagged ASSUMPTION
